## Design

### 2026-10-07 – I made the schematic for the Starbie using KiCad. I started by downloading the care package and importing the Seeed_Studio_XIAO_Series.kicad_sym file as a symbol library and the Imported Parts.pretty

**1.25h**

I made the schematic for the Starbie using KiCad. I started by downloading the care package and importing the Seeed_Studio_XIAO_Series.kicad_sym file as a symbol library and the Imported Parts.pretty file as a footprint library. I later found out that I had incorrectly imported the footprint library and accidentally moved the project file location there, so I moved the files out and imported the footprint library the right way. I then made the schematics for the ESP32 C3, the buttons, the environment sensor, the OLED, and the MPU6050. I originally got stuck on creating net labels when starting with the ESP32 C3 schematic, because I thought the rectangle and text for organization were the net label, but after looking at the images in the guide and the elements made by pressing L, I was able to clear up what net labels were and finish the schematics. I used rectangles and text boxes to organize them in the same way that they were in the guide, then I assigned footprints for each element and saved the project.

### 2026-10-07 – I made and routed the board for the components. I started by making the outline of the board, but at first I accidentally made the outline on the front wiring layer rather than the edge cuts layer, an

**1h**

I made and routed the board for the components. I started by making the outline of the board, but at first I accidentally made the outline on the front wiring layer rather than the edge cuts layer, and I made it with triangles which I believe you can't do. I then rearranged the components and began routing the connections. I wasn't able to make all the connections at first so I rearranged the components to look like they do in the guide. I had to flip the resistor to the other side to make the connections easier. I still struggled with making all the connections, so I watched the tutorial on how to make a ground plane, but I then figured out how to route on the other side of the board and chose to route all the ground wirings this way. This allowed me to finish the connections, after which I ran the DRC and confirmed there were no errors. Finally, I wrote my name on the board and drew a smiley face that was accidentally on the wrong layer at first.

### 2026-10-10 – I worked on the code for the Starbie in this session. First I downloaded the latest Arduino IDE. Then I added Espressif as an additional board manager and installed the esp32 board by Espressif System

**1h**

I worked on the code for the Starbie in this session. First I downloaded the latest Arduino IDE. Then I added Espressif as an additional board manager and installed the esp32 board by Espressif Systems. I installed the Adafruit GFX Library library, the Adafruit SSD1306 library, the Adafruit MPU6050 library, and the DHT sensor library library as well as their dependencies. Then I downloaded the Starbie.ino file and moved it to be in my Starbie folder. I opened Starbie.ino and added the void drawSparkle() function and the extra accompanying if condition in drawPet(). I uploaded my Starbie files to my Github repository, then found a tutorial online for how to export gerber files from KiCad. I realized I had put my name and design for the PCB on the wrong layer again, so I moved to the correct layer, then created drill files and plotted the gerber files. Finally, I compressed all the gerber files and uploaded them to my repository.
